question.problem:
Consider the following inhomogeneous system of linear differential equations:

$$
{x}^{′}(t)=[\begin{aligned}2/5 & -6/5 \\ -6/5 & -7/5\end{aligned}]x(t)+[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 4\end{aligned}]
$$

The complementary solution to this system is given by

$$
{x}_{c}(t)={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]{e}^{-2t}+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1\end{aligned}]{e}^{t},\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R.
$$

Then, the general solution of the system can be written as 
$x(t)={x}_{c}(t)+{x}_{p}(t),$
where ${x}_{p}(t)$ is a particular solution. Determine the form of the particular solution ${x}_{p}(t).$

current_example.worked_solution:
Recall that the general solution of an inhomogeneous system can be written as 

$$
\mathbf{x}(t)=\mathbf{x}_c(t)+\mathbf{x}_p(t)
$$

where $\mathbf{x}_c(t)$ is the complementary solution (solution of the corresponding homogeneous system) and $\mathbf{x}_p(t)$ is a particular solution.

The forcing term
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14219741/assets/959244c2867832f554e15fde048a1187578e7c4464a2eb835c2282a28a21fc7e.svg)
of the inhomogeneous system of ODEs is sinusoidal. Therefore, we assume that the particular solution is also sinusoidal, i.e.
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14219741/assets/2bdb3bbbb542bb72cb5c3368e28f2aec3ab8a3314f5c81a9fb7bb45141cfb26a.svg)
where $a_1,a_2,b_1,b_2$ are constants that are to be determined.
